hypotheses.justification: `b` is not used anywhere in the statement except its own binder; the proof uses it only as a reference basis of V for the Wronskian W. Without it there are two cases. If w = 0, the left-hand side is an empty sum, hence 0, and the inequality holds trivially. If w ≥ 1, set b := e ⟨0, _⟩, a basis of the same V indexed by Fin h. The existing proof then works verbatim: `localOrder` uses `wronskian_order_at` and `wronskian_basis_rootMultiplicity d b (e i) (a i) hV`, which accepts any two bases. The final degree bound uses `hV (b j)`, `natDegree_wronskian_le`, `sum_rootMultiplicity_le_natDegree` and injectivity of `a`, none of which depends on where b came from. So the theorem stays true and provable without `b` (case split on w, i.e. on Fin w being empty).
